name: sar-logic-functional-gates
description: Gate-level replay of sim/sar-logic-functional/ (issue #11's exhaustive SAR-controller functional verification, DR-0014 bottom-plate sampling) against the SYNTHESIZED gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v, issue #272) instead of the ideal rung-1 XSPICE sar_ctrl_a model, over the block's ratified PVT corner grid (issue #273, DR-0023 follow-on (a) continuation).
claim: README.md#target-specification -- Latency/conversion-timing row and Interface row, re-checked on the real synthesized gate netlist instead of the ideal rung-1 model. Also re-checks DR-0011's mode-dependent bit-trial switching and DR-0014's two-phase sample/four-leg one-hot invariant on real gf180mcu standard cells rather than ideal XSPICE digital primitives.

err_se_max.description: THE FUNCTIONAL CHECK, single-ended, UNCHANGED FROM THE RUNG-1 IDEAL SIBLING (sim/sar-logic-functional/testbench/tb.json) -- same +/-0.5 LSB bound, not relaxed for the gate-level netlist (CLAUDE.md). Largest positive deviation, over the run, between the converted code and the closed-form ideal code of the sample that produced it, evaluated inside every drdy window.

err_se_min.description: same check, largest negative deviation, unchanged bound.

code_se_max.description: COVERAGE WITNESS, upper end -- WIDENED relative to the rung-1 sibling's [1022.5, 1023.5] because this deck's conversion count is deliberately reduced to 64 (gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own docstring: ~7.9 s wall-clock per conversion measured on real gf180mcu transistors, so the full 1024-conversion sweep does not fit inside a tractable full-mos-grid budget). The ramp still spans the full range 0..1023, but the LAST conversion's own acquisition instant lands at ~63.19 us of the 64 us run rather than at the very end, so the highest code actually held and compared is measured (not assumed) to be close to but short of 1023 -- this bound is set from that measurement, not guessed.

code_se_min.description: COVERAGE WITNESS, lower end -- WIDENED for the same reduced-nconv reason as code_se_max: the FIRST conversion's own acquisition instant lands near ~0.19 us into the run (the ramp starts at half an LSB, and the first held sample is close to but not exactly at the range's bottom edge, unlike the rung-1 sibling's per-code 1-conversion granularity). Measured, not assumed -- see this experiment's records.

sw_conflict_se.description: SWITCH-DRIVER ONE-HOT INVARIANT -- bound REVISED from the rung-1 sibling's 0.02 by DR-0027 (`spec/decision-records/DR-0027-gate-decode-one-hot-hazard-budget.md`, issue #298), which accepts a disclosed, bounded real-hazard budget for this synthesized-netlist check rather than a synthesis-level delay-balancing fix. Root cause (issue #295, `../investigations/20260916-issue-295-sw-conflict-root-cause.md`): `klt synthesize` De Morgan-folds `sar_ctrl.v`'s shared `smpb` inverter into each `rel_n_<weight><side>` cell, opening a real ~143-165 ps four-leg one-hot gap (a floating bottom-plate node, not a rail-to-rail short) on every acquisition-window-closing edge. DR-0027's evidence (RC-time-constant/leakage order-of-magnitude argument, plus `err_se_max/min` reading exactly 0 on every corner already measured) is why 15 -- roughly 50% headroom over the worst value measured so far (9.99828, `fs_27c_3.30v`, `sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/records/20260915-214338-912a8ec.md`) -- is a real ceiling, not a rubber stamp: it still catches a genuine further regression (e.g. an overlap-type defect).

nside_cells_se.description: DR-0011 MODE RULE, single-ended half -- bound REVISED from 0.02 by DR-0027 (same root cause as `sw_conflict_se`, smaller magnitude: a 1.2-1.7%-of-VDD transient glitch on the logically-constant-0 n-side nodes, coincident with the same `sel_in_n` edge). ~50% headroom over the worst value measured so far (0.0644431, `ff_27c_3.30v`).

err_df_max.description: THE FUNCTIONAL CHECK, differential -- unchanged bound from the rung-1 sibling.

err_df_min.description: same check, largest negative deviation, unchanged bound.

code_df_max.description: COVERAGE WITNESS, differential upper end -- widened for the same reduced-nconv reason as code_se_max.

code_df_min.description: COVERAGE WITNESS, differential lower end -- widened for the same reduced-nconv reason as code_se_min.

sw_conflict_df.description: The same four-leg one-hot invariant in differential mode -- bound REVISED from 0.02 by DR-0027 (see `sw_conflict_se`'s description for the root cause and rationale). ~50% headroom over the worst value measured so far (13.0045, `ss_27c_3.30v`).

nside_cells_df.description: DR-0011 MODE RULE, differential half -- unchanged bound.

conv_period_ns.description: CONVERSION CADENCE -- unchanged bound. Measured over 55 conversions (RISE=5..RISE=60 on se_drdy, out of 64 total, skipping a few at each end) instead of the rung-1 sibling's 1000 (out of 1024) -- the averaging span shrinks with nconv, the bound itself does not.

acq_window_ns.description: DR-0014 ACQUISITION WINDOW -- bound REVISED by DR-0030 (spec/decision-records/DR-0030-functional-deck-acquisition-isolation-bounds.md, issue #324) from the inherited 185..190 ns, to DR-0028's derived pair, which the gate-level TIMING sibling sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ already carries. Averaged over 60 whole conversions (FROM=2u TO=62u) instead of the rung-1 sibling's 1000. THE LIMITS HERE ARE DERIVED FROM THE MARGIN, NOT FROM A MEASUREMENT, and they are NOT the rung-1 sibling's any more: DR-0030's rule is that these limits follow the DUT, not the deck, so a deck wrapping the synthesized gf180mcu netlist bounds a physical margin with a real PVT spread while a deck wrapping the rung-1 ideal XSPICE model guards a deterministic generator. LOWER LIMIT 175.0 ns = the settling floor: DR-0013's input-pin redistribution kick is 1024*C_in/(C_in+C_pin) = 83.06 LSB at the worst permitted C_pin = 100 pF, recovered with tau_in <= 30 ns (DR-0013's contract ceiling), so allocating 0.25 LSB -- half the 1/2-LSB settling criterion, to keep the term negligible rather than merely legal -- to the un-recovered residual at the sampling instant requires 30*ln(83.06/0.25) = 174.17 ns, rounded UP so the limit is never looser than its derivation. UPPER LIMIT 218.7 ns = DR-0003's 4-clock sample phase (4 x 62.5 = 250 ns) less iso_gap_ns's 31.25 ns ordering floor, rounded DOWN; because acq_window_ns + iso_gap_ns IS that 250 ns phase to within half a nanosecond at every PVT point measured, each upper limit is the other measurement's floor restated rather than an independent number. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT: every input (DR-0013's tau_in/C_pin contract, DR-0003's 62.5 ns phase, the 1/2-LSB criterion) is a spec quantity P&R does not change, so this is one limit pre- AND post-layout, not a pre-layout number to be re-baselined. IT IS ALSO STILL THE WHOLE-CLOCK GUARD THE INHERITED WINDOW CLAIMED TO BE: a dropped sample clock (125.0 ns) misses the floor by 50 ns and an added one (250.0 ns) misses the ceiling by 31.3 ns. Worst slack on THIS deck's committed records: 4.74 ns at fs_27c_3.30v (179.743 ns, records/20260917-044312-c7ff0ff.md) -- but this deck has only ever scored the 5-point process axis at 27C/3.30V, so the GOVERNING pre-layout slack is DR-0028's 1.93 ns at fs_125c_2.97v from the 45-point sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/ grid, and a full grid here should be expected to land near that.

iso_gap_ns.description: DR-0014's TWO-PHASE SAMPLE, single-ended loop -- and the SIGN is the ordering claim. Bound REVISED by DR-0030 (issue #324) from the inherited 60..65 ns to DR-0028's derived pair, for the same reason as acq_window_ns above. LOWER LIMIT 31.3 ns = the ordering floor, half of one DR-0003 clock phase (31.25 ns, rounded UP). POSITIVE means sel_in_n falls LAST -- the input legs turn off onto an already-isolated node, which is the entire mechanism of DR-0014 -- and both real failure modes are a whole clock phase in size (second phase DROPPED -> 0 ns; the two phases SWAPPED -> -62.5 ns), so a half-phase floor still fails decisively on both, by 31.25 ns and 93.75 ns. UPPER LIMIT 75.0 ns = the 250 ns sample phase less acq_window_ns's 175.0 ns settling floor: excess isolation is missing acquisition. LAYOUT-INDEPENDENT, for the same reason as acq_window_ns. Worst slack on this deck's committed records: 26.02 ns on the floor (57.3198 ns at sf_27c_3.30v) and 4.60 ns on the ceiling (70.3956 ns at fs_27c_3.30v), records/20260917-044312-c7ff0ff.md; the governing pre-layout figures remain DR-0028's 22.0 ns / 1.67 ns from the 45-point grid. The asymmetry is the finding: input settling is the binding constraint on the two-phase sample, and the ordering claim itself is robust across the whole PVT box.

iso_gap_df_ns.description: The same isolation gap on the DIFFERENTIAL loop -- bound REVISED by DR-0030 (issue #324) from the inherited 60..65 ns to the SAME derived pair as iso_gap_ns above. DR-0028 correctly noted it had no gate-level TIMING evidence for this measurement (the timing decks do not measure it at all); DR-0030 transfers the DERIVATION rather than evidence, and the derivation contains no term that distinguishes the loops -- it is DR-0003's 62.5 ns clock phase, the sub-nanosecond requirement that the top-plate switch be fully off before the bottom plates move, and the 250 ns sample phase, and DR-0014's fourth leg is deliberately NOT mode-gated, so the differential loop acquires through the same two controls in the same phase against the same requirement. WHY THIS CHECK IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH iso_gap_ns: if someone later gated sel_in by mode -- which looks like a tidy-up, and which would make the two sides' sampling switches differ, the one asymmetry bottom-plate sampling cannot cancel -- this number goes to 0 or about -62.5 while the single-ended one does not, and the 31.3 ns floor fails that by 31.25 ns / 93.75 ns. WHAT THE WIDER BOUND GIVES UP, STATED: two loops bounded independently at 31.3..75.0 can part company by tens of nanoseconds with both still passing, where 60..65 tripped on about 5 ns. That is a real loss of a small-asymmetry guard, accepted per DR-0030's Consequences because the failure this check exists for is a whole-clock event that the floor still catches; restoring it properly needs the DIFFERENCE measured directly (it tracks iso_gap_ns to <= 0.0004 ns at every point committed under sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/records/, so it would carry a genuinely tight bound), which is a new measurement expression and is tracked as issue #334 rather than done here.

iso_skew_ns.description: ISSUE #334: THE DIFFERENCE iso_gap_ns and iso_gap_df_ns's own descriptions name and defer -- (iso_av_df-iso_av)*1000, i.e. iso_gap_df_ns minus iso_gap_ns computed directly rather than by subtracting two independently-rounded checks. WHY ITS BOUND CAN BE TIGHT WHERE THE PER-LOOP BOUNDS CANNOT: iso_gap_ns/iso_gap_df_ns each bound a physical margin with a real +/-10 ns PVT spread (DR-0028/DR-0030), so each needs the wide 31.3..75.0 ns window that spread demands. The skew between them carries none of that spread, because both loops sample the input through the SAME two controls (samp_tp_n, sel_in_n) in the SAME 250 ns sample phase, driven from the SAME phase sequencer edge -- any PVT shift that moves one loop's isolation gap moves the other's by (to first order) the same amount, so it cancels in the difference and the expectation is exactly zero, not merely small. The residual is not zero in practice only because the two loops are physically distinct instances (the differential loop switches all 18 cells against the single-ended loop's 9, a real fanout/loading difference on internal decode nodes) measured with the same AVG-over-N-whole-conversions instrument as iso_gap_ns/iso_gap_df_ns, which floors this at the instrument's own resolution rather than at anything the ordering claim itself limits. LOWER/UPPER LIMIT +/-0.01 ns: derived, not copied from the issue's own worked example -- across every scored point committed under sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/records/ (20260915-214338-912a8ec, 20260916-043850-e5440a0, 20260917-044312-c7ff0ff, 11 rows spanning the tt/ff/ss/fs/sf process axis at 27C/3.30V, including the fs_27c/sf_27c rows that fail iso_gap_ns/iso_gap_df_ns outright), the two numbers agree to <= 0.0004 ns -- so +/-0.01 ns is 25x that worst-observed residual (headroom for the temperature/supply axes this deck has not yet scored a full grid on, per iso_gap_ns's own note), while still three orders of magnitude tighter than iso_gap_ns/iso_gap_df_ns's own 43.7 ns window and multiple orders of magnitude below either real failure mode this check would also see indirectly (a mode-gated sel_in drives this to about -62.5 or +62.5 ns, not a few ps). SIGN IS NOT A CLAIM HERE (unlike iso_gap_ns): the two loops are nominally identical, not ordered, so the bound is symmetric about zero rather than one-sided.

notes: REDUCED CONVERSION COUNT, STATED RATHER THAN HIDDEN: this deck runs 64 conversions per loop, not the rung-1 ideal sibling's exhaustive 1024. gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own docstring records the measurement that justifies this: ~7.9 s of wall-clock per simulated conversion on the real gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (two-loop composition, nominal corner) -- roughly three orders of magnitude slower than the rung-1 ideal-XSPICE sibling's cost, because ngspice is now solving ~2700 real 6V-oxide transistors per loop rather than free digital events. At nconv=1024 a single PVT point would cost ~2.25 hours, making the full ratified mos-corner-grid (45 points) cost on the order of 100 hours of serial CPU-time for this deck alone. nconv=64 keeps the FULL grid (the claim #273 actually exists to answer -- does process/temperature/supply skew move any of these numbers) tractable within a single verification pass, at the cost of testing a coarser (but still full-range, both-ends) subset of the 1024 possible codes rather than every one of them -- the rung-1 sibling already owns exhaustive per-code coverage and runs unmodified on every PR.

Consequently the coverage-witness checks (code_se_max/min, code_df_max/min) are WIDENED relative to the rung-1 sibling, per each check's own description above -- this is a disclosed, measured widening of a coverage witness bound, not a relaxation of the actual functional pass/fail bounds (err_*, conv_period_ns), which are UNCHANGED from sim/sar-logic-functional/testbench/tb.json.

TWO FAMILIES OF BOUND NO LONGER MATCH THE RUNG-1 SIBLING, BOTH BY DECISION AND BOTH WITH A RECORD BEHIND THEM -- this note used to claim every functional/timing bound here was identical to sim/sar-logic-functional/testbench/tb.json's, and that claim is now false. (1) sw_conflict_se/sw_conflict_df/nside_cells_se carry DR-0027's disclosed real-hazard budget (0.02 -> 15/20/0.1), per the ISSUE #298 / DR-0027 note below. (2) acq_window_ns/iso_gap_ns/iso_gap_df_ns carry DR-0028's derived margin bounds (185..190 -> 175.0..218.7 and 60..65 -> 31.3..75.0), applied to this deck by spec/decision-records/DR-0030-functional-deck-acquisition-isolation-bounds.md (issue #324). DR-0030's rule is that these three limits follow the RUNG OF THE DUT, not the deck: this deck and sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ wrap the synthesized gf180mcu netlist, whose real +/-10 ns process spread is a physical margin to bound, while sim/sar-logic-functional/ and sim/sar-logic-timing/ wrap the rung-1 ideal XSPICE model, which has no process axis and whose tighter windows are therefore correct regression guards on a deterministic generator. Re-read against these limits the acq/iso rows of every record under records/ pass, INCLUDING the fs_27c_3.30v / sf_27c_3.30v rows of 20260917-044312-c7ff0ff.md that this deck was failing -- DR-0030's Consequences states that plainly and gives the evidence for why it is a corrected bound rather than a convenient one. Nothing was re-run or re-scored: the records keep their text and their verdicts as written, per sim/'s append-only rule.

PVT GRID: unlike the rung-1 ideal sibling (no PDK device models, so process/temperature cannot move anything and only tt/27C is run), this deck wraps a real synthesized gf180mcu netlist and is therefore swept over the full ratified mos corner-set (tt/ff/ss/fs/sf) x -40/27/125 C x +/-10% supply -- 45 points -- exactly the grid #273 was filed to run.

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model is UNCHANGED from the rung-1 sibling (same _loop() composition in gen_sar_logic.py) -- only the DUT subckt sar_ctrl_a changed, from the ideal XSPICE model to the real synthesized netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/gate_netlist_to_spice.py's translation of design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v). What this record newly proves beyond the rung-1 sibling: the same closed-loop functional behaviour holds when the sequencing, switch decode and output register are IMPLEMENTED as real gf180mcu standard cells rather than ideal digital primitives, across process/temperature/supply.

SEEDING: design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note' applies here (a real dffq_1 standard cell carries no reset pin) -- every loop in this deck drives its own start net high for 2 whole clock periods from t=0 (gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's START_PULSE_CLOCKS) before dropping it, so the ph ring's one-hot invariant is established before any other output is trusted. The rung-1 ideal sibling never needed this (its sar_ctrl_a model seeds ph15 with an XSPICE ic=1 instead).

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour, unchanged from the rung-1 sibling's own disclosure.

ISSUE #282 (RESOLVED): the first attempted run surfaced a genuine, reproducible non-convergence blocker: ngspice did not converge the translated 181-cell sar_ctrl_a gate netlist to a valid digital operating point at all -- even a combinational node whose value is provably unique given the applied stimulus (the OR gate feeding ph0's flip-flop D input, forced high by `start`) settled near 0 V instead of VDD, with only small clk-correlated capacitive ripple, for the whole run. Root cause: the supply net every standard cell binds (`vdd_gate`) is supplied from OUTSIDE the emitted `.subckt sar_ctrl_a` -- nothing inside the subckt drives it -- so without an explicit `.global vdd_gate` declaration, SPICE scoped it LOCALLY to each cell instance, leaving the entire DUT unpowered. `design/sar-logic/flow/gate_netlist_to_spice.py` now emits that `.global` declaration (plus a structural guard, `_assert_external_nets_reachable`, that refuses to emit a subckt where an externally-supplied net would be left locally scoped), and `gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py` re-checks the property on the assembled deck. Validated on a small, standalone, non-closed-loop probe deck (sar_ctrl_a driven directly, no CDAC loop) before this fix landed here: the previously-degenerate node now reads exactly 3.3 V, and vdd_gate itself reads 3.3 V throughout, confirming the DUT reaches a trustworthy digital operating point.

CORNER-GRID RUNS ARE RECORDED HERE: this experiment has populated records/, corners/ and netlist-snapshots/ directories, and its first corner-grid run is sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/records/20260915-214338-912a8ec.md, executed under issue #289. Read the individual record for what any given run actually measured and which corner points it covered -- this note does not summarise results. HISTORY (kept because it explains the gap between this deck being written and its first grid being recorded): the deck initially carried no corner-grid run because of #282's non-convergence blocker (the missing `.global vdd_gate` declaration described in the note above, now fixed); after that fix it still carried none for a DIFFERENT reason, namely that actually executing the full 45-point mos grid for this deck is a substantial compute-cost undertaking in its own right (see the REDUCED CONVERSION COUNT note above: ~8.4 CPU-minutes/point at nconv=64, ~6+ hours serial CPU-time for the full grid) that #282's own session could not complete on top of severe, measured host contention that session hit (a single nominal-corner point took over an hour of wall-clock time against an ~8.4-minute CPU estimate, on a host reporting sustained load averages of 27-39 on 28 cores). That pure execution/recording follow-on was tracked as issue #289, which has since run the grid -- it never reopened the convergence question #282 answered.

ISSUE #298 / DR-0027: #289's own corner-grid run (sim/sar-logic-functional-gates/records/20260915-214338-912a8ec.md) measured a severe, corner-independent violation of the sw_conflict_se/df/nside_cells_se checks above. #295's investigation (../investigations/20260916-issue-295-sw-conflict-root-cause.md) root-caused it to a genuine, real (not idealized) combinational hazard: klt synthesize De Morgan-folds sar_ctrl.v's shared smpb inverter into each rel_n_<weight><side> cell, opening a real ~143-165 ps four-leg one-hot gap (a floating switch node, not a shorted one) on every acquisition-window-closing edge. Issue #298 evaluated the physical significance of that gap and chose, per spec/decision-records/DR-0027-gate-decode-one-hot-hazard-budget.md, to accept it as a disclosed, bounded real-hazard budget -- revising sw_conflict_se/sw_conflict_df/nside_cells_se's bounds above (0.02 -> 15/20/0.1) -- rather than a synthesis-level delay-balancing fix, because the ratified synthesis flow (design/sar-logic/flow/synth_sar_ctrl.py, DR-0023 follow-on (a)) carries no timing/SDC methodology to durably enforce one. err_se_max/min/err_df_max/min (the actual conversion-correctness check) are unaffected by this change and already read exactly 0 on every corner recorded above.
